explanations.explanation: It's an easy guess, since Joseph does sit on the Council. But Luke says he “…had not consented to their decision or action.” (Luke 23:51) So he had a seat at that table, but he didn't sign off on what they did. I think that took quiet courage.

That's right, friend. Joseph is a Council member, but Luke says he “…had not consented to their decision or action.” (Luke 23:51) He held a seat there without going along with them. I think that's a lonely spot to be in.

Joseph of Arimathea, the Council member, goes to Pilate, the governor, and asks for the body of Jesus. That's the whole request, plain and simple. Then Luke tells us what Joseph does next, and he does it with care. I think this was a man who knew exactly what he came for.

Funny enough, a guard does come up later, but not from Joseph. In Matthew, the chief priests and Pharisees go to Pilate, the governor, to ask for the tomb to be made secure (Matthew 27:62-66). Joseph of Arimathea, the Council member, asks for something else in Luke. He asks for the body of Jesus.

The garments of Jesus do get talked about, but at the cross. The soldiers divided His garments by casting lots (Luke 23:34). When Joseph of Arimathea, the Council member, stands before Pilate, the governor, he asks for something far more important. He asks for the body of Jesus (Luke 23:52).

explanations.answer: In a tomb cut into the rock
explanations.explanation: Joseph wraps the body in linen and places it in a tomb cut into the rock. Luke tells us exactly where, so there's no guessing. The women from Galilee saw the tomb and how His body was placed (Luke 23:55). I think Joseph handled it with great care.

Machpelah is a real burial cave. It's where Abraham, the father of Israel's people, buried his wife Sarah (Genesis 23:19). But Joseph's tomb in Luke is a different place. It's a tomb cut into the rock.

explanations.answer: In the field of the potter
explanations.explanation: The Potter's Field is a real burial place in Matthew. The chief priests bought it to bury foreigners (Matthew 27:7). But that isn't where Joseph lays Jesus. Luke says he places the body in a tomb cut into the rock.

explanations.answer: They rest as the commandment says
explanations.explanation: Luke says they “…rested on the Sabbath, according to the commandment.” (Luke 23:56) The spices are ready, and they still wait. They don't rush the work. They rest first, and then they go back to the tomb.

explanations.answer: They keep watch outside the city
explanations.explanation: Luke doesn't say anything about a watch outside the city. He says they rested on the Sabbath, “…according to the commandment.” (Luke 23:56) Their spices were all ready, and they still waited. I think that waiting was hard.

That's right, friend. Luke says that when the women entered, “…they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.” (Luke 24:3) They came with spices, ready to care for Him. And they find the tomb without the body.

explanations.answer: They bow their faces to the ground
explanations.explanation: Luke says the women “…bowed their faces to the ground in terror…” (Luke 24:5) Two men in radiant apparel just appeared beside them. That's a lot for one morning. I'd be bowing too, friend.

explanations.answer: They drop the spices and cry out
explanations.explanation: Luke doesn't say they dropped the spices or cried out. What he says is that they “…bowed their faces to the ground in terror…” (Luke 24:5) Two men in radiant apparel were suddenly beside them. I think any of us would have frozen up.

explanations.answer: They reach out to touch the men
explanations.explanation: That's not what Luke tells us. He says the women “…bowed their faces to the ground in terror…” (Luke 24:5) Two men in radiant apparel were suddenly beside them. Luke doesn't say they reached out to touch anyone. He says they bowed down with their faces to the ground.
The two men say, “He is not here; He has risen!” (Luke 24:6) That's the biggest news there is. The tomb is empty because Jesus is risen. They don't offer any other explanation.

Joseph is the one who placed Jesus in the tomb, but the two men don't say he moved Him. They say, “He is not here; He has risen!” (Luke 24:6) That's the news they give the women. Joseph doesn't come into it.
The two men say nothing about soldiers. What they say is, “He is not here; He has risen!” (Luke 24:6) That's the answer to the empty tomb. Jesus rose.

Jesus said the Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, be crucified, and “…on the third day rise again.” (Luke 24:7) Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). He told them this ahead of time. And the two men tell the women to remember it.

The two men quote Jesus differently. He said the Son of Man would be crucified, and “…on the third day rise again.” (Luke 24:7) Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). It's the third day, not the seventh.

Forty days does show up later, when the risen Jesus appears to His followers over a period of forty days (Acts 1:3). But that isn't the day in His words here. Jesus said the Son of Man would “…on the third day rise again.” (Luke 24:7) Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10).

That's right, friend. Luke says, “But their words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe the women.” (Luke 24:11) The women reported it, and to the apostles it seemed like nonsense. I think that was hard on the women.

Luke says Peter “…got up and ran to the tomb.” (Luke 24:12) Peter is one of the apostles, and the women's words had seemed like nonsense to them (Luke 24:11). But he doesn't sit still. He gets up and runs.

Joseph is the Council member who laid Jesus in the tomb, but Luke has Peter go somewhere else. Peter, one of the apostles, “…got up and ran to the tomb.” (Luke 24:12) Luke sends him straight to the tomb. That's where he goes.
